obligation: Bank recall request for each diverted payment
trigger: A payment (ACH or wire) is suspected to have gone to an account controlled by an attacker
deadline: Immediately on suspicion. IC3: 'time is of the essence'
notify: The group's bank fraud desk (Property AP payment); the owner and each tenant are asked to call their own banks (inbound payments)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - highest priority action; not a legal duty
notifying_entity: Group Treasurer (Property AP payment); Construction project executive's manager with the Group Treasurer (owner payment); Property Controller (tenants)

obligation: Complaint to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
trigger: Any business email compromise with a fraudulent transfer or attempt
deadline: As soon as possible, regardless of the amount; IC3 may help freeze funds
notify: IC3 (www.ic3.gov); local FBI field office given the amounts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but required by POL-03 4.10

obligation: DoD cyber incident report (covered defense information in the compromised mailbox)
trigger: A cyber incident affects covered defense information: the compromised mailbox held CUI-marked drawings from a DoD design-build project
deadline: Rapidly report within 72 hours of discovery
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil (medium assurance certificate held by the Director of Federal Contracts Compliance)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Cris Santos Construction, LLC is the prime on the affected DoD contract
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Construction, LLC (Director of Federal Contracts Compliance)

obligation: Malicious software submission
trigger: Malicious software isolated in connection with the reported incident
deadline: When discovered and isolated; follow DoD instructions (do not send to the Contracting Officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if malware is found (none expected in a mailbox-only compromise)

obligation: Media preservation and DoD access
trigger: A cyber incident is reported under 252.204-7012(c)
deadline: Preserve images of affected systems and relevant monitoring and packet capture data for at least 90 days from the report; give DoD access if requested
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Subcontractor report number to the prime (design-build)
trigger: A&E, as Construction's subcontractor on a design-build project, has a cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Subcontractor reports to DoD within 72 hours and gives the incident report number to the prime as soon as practicable
notify: Construction (prime) through the Director of Federal Contracts Compliance
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario (A&E systems not affected). Shown because the path inside the group is not yet written down (POAM-004)

obligation: CMMC status currency after the incident
trigger: The incident shows that a CMMC Level 1 requirement for the PDPP scope (which includes SYS-G5 email) is no longer met
deadline: Before relying on the status for any award or the 2027-01-20 annual affirmation: restore the requirement and re-assess
notify: Internal: Construction division president (Affirming Official); Group General Counsel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the final clause has no separate incident notice duty

obligation: Correct SAM EFT information and alert the federal payment office
trigger: The attacker changed SAM EFT data, or a federal payment is missing
deadline: Immediately. If EFT information was incorrect or revised within 30 days of the Government's release of payment and the funds have left the payment office, the Government is deemed to have paid
notify: SAM; Contracting Officer and paying office for each affected contract
applies_at_this_tier: Check in this scenario (SAM roles reviewed; no change found in the exercise)

obligation: Pay subcontractors on federal contracts despite a diverted payment
trigger: A payment meant for a subcontractor on a federal job went to an attacker
deadline: Subcontractor must still be paid within 7 days of the prime's receipt of the Government's payment; interest penalty for late payment
notify: The real subcontractor (after call-back verification of its bank details)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the Property AP fraud involves a subcontractor on a federal job (it does not in this scenario; it would for Construction AP)

obligation: Owner notice of a compromised payment channel
trigger: An owner received false remittance instructions from a group mailbox or lookalike domain
deadline: Immediately by phone to the owner's AP contact on file, then in writing
notify: The owner's AP and project representative; all owners with a pay application in the last 60 days get a confirmation letter
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not a statutory duty
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Construction, LLC (project executive's manager)

obligation: Tenant notice of lookalike remittance letters
trigger: Tenants received rent remittance letters from a lookalike domain
deadline: Immediately by phone to each tenant's AP contact on file, then a letter to all about 1,600 tenants restating the remittance rule
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and protective, not a statutory duty

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Unauthorized access to personal information of Florida residents: name plus Social Security number in certified payrolls; the project executive's email address plus password (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days; law enforcement delay only on written request
notify: Each affected Florida resident (about 1,240 craft workers and the project executive)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - certified payrolls with full Social Security numbers were in the mailbox
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Construction, LLC (Group General Counsel)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 1,240 Florida residents
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Construction, LLC (Group General Counsel)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 1,860 individuals in total
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Construction, LLC (Group General Counsel)

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (instead of individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the entity reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or financial harm
deadline: Document in writing; keep 5 years; give to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Not expected: the attacker read the mailbox for weeks and the files contain full Social Security numbers

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the covered entity (worked example)
trigger: Corporate shared services runs the email suite for the subsidiaries; counsel treats it conservatively as a third-party agent
deadline: No later than 10 days after the third-party agent's determination
notify: The affected subsidiary (Cris Santos Construction, LLC)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - documented on the bridge on Day 0 so the subsidiary's clock is never later than corporate's

obligation: Other state breach notification laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of other states (about 620 craft workers in 3 other states)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days); some states require attorney general or regulator notice
notify: Affected residents; state attorneys general or regulators where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Construction, LLC (Group General Counsel)

obligation: Subcontractor notice about their workers' payroll data
trigger: Subcontractors' certified payrolls with their workers' Social Security numbers were in the mailbox
deadline: Promptly, before individual notices go out, so subcontractors can answer their workers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and practical

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines the incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination). Determine materiality without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the disclosure committee decides; escalation within 24 hours (POL-03 4.6)
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. (disclosure committee)

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - consider the incident and lessons learned in the next description

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
deadline: Per policy; the social engineering sublimit ($10 million) requires prompt notice and proof of verification procedures
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual. Use panel counsel and forensics

obligation: Surety notice
citation: General indemnity agreement with the surety (contract)
trigger: A loss that could affect working capital or the ability to pay subcontractors on bonded projects
deadline: Per the agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Check with counsel - contractual

obligation: PCI DSS incident response for parking (acquirer and card brands)
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10; merchant agreement with the acquirer (contract)
trigger: Suspected compromise of cardholder data at parking facilities
deadline: Per the merchant agreement and card brand rules (not verified in this sample)
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered: business email compromise does not touch cardholder data, which stays with the provider

obligation: TSSI managed-service and digital twin client notices
trigger: Client facility security details or client data in the compromised mailbox
deadline: Per each client agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Check in analysis: none found in this scenario
notifying_entity: Systems Integration Director; A&E digital services director

obligation: Report discovery of covered telecommunications equipment or services
trigger: Covered equipment identified in a system during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered by business email compromise. Listed because the matrix is group-wide (used for the 2026-08-12 finding, POAM-029)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary until then). The proposed scope would reach DFARS 252.204-7012 contractors

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Not for business email compromise (no ransom). Applies only if an extortion demand follows
